title: Envelope
description: The two frames on the wire. An Entry is one line of the log, and the log's envelope IS the event: what the gateway streams to a subscriber and what it stores are the same bytes. A Command is what an app sends the gateway.

Entry.description: One line of a call's log, or of an agent's log when call is null. seq is written before control returns, so two readers never disagree about order.

seq.description: The entry's place in its log, starting at 1, never reused. The cursor a reader resumes from.

ts.description: When the entry was written, unix seconds with fractions.

call.description: The call this entry belongs to. Null for entries about the agent itself: registered, configured, pong, an error outside any call.

agent.description: The agent's slug, as it registered: clinica-norte.

type.description: Which event this is, dotted: call.started, turn.user, metrics.llm. The closed list is the events/ folder.

ephemeral.description: True for entries a store may drop and a slow reader may miss without harm: interim transcripts, VAD health, replay markers. False for everything the truth is made of.

data.description: The event's payload, whose shape is the event's own schema under events/<type>.json.

Command.description: One instruction from an app to the gateway over its WebSocket. The gateway answers with the events the command produces, or with an error naming the command's id.

type.description: Which command this is, dotted: state.set, call.dial, ping. The closed list is the commands/ folder.

agent.description: The agent this command speaks for. A socket may serve several agents.

call.description: The call the command is about, or null for commands about the agent: register, configure, dial, ping.

id.description: The app's own id for the command, echoed back on an error so the app knows which one failed.

data.description: The command's payload, whose shape is the command's own schema under commands/<type>.json.
